**What's new**

- Fixed: loading a save could end the game with "Failed allocating buffer with error ErrorOutOfDeviceMemory" when other programs held a lot of video memory, released builds too. One draw there reads 2.4 GB the game wrote at once, which was uploaded through a 2.5 GB staging buffer; uploads over 256 MB now go through staging memory of that size, a part at a time. Buffers and images that don't fit the memory budget the driver reports are now allocated past it, which the driver makes room for by moving memory out, instead of ending the game.
- New experimental setting, off by default: **Run Compute Rings on a Second Queue (Experimental)** (`async_compute` in the config). It runs the work of the game's compute rings on a second queue of the GPU beside the graphics work, with the uploads it needs and the copies back of what it wrote. In the park, 99% of those dispatches run there and the graphics queue's GPU time halves, from 11-14 to 6 ms a frame, but two in three of them still wait for graphics work in flight, and the frame rate stayed about the same on the test machine below (65.6 fps with it, 69.2 without, on average over three rounds each, rounds with it varying from 56 to 76 fps), where the emulator's GPU thread is the limit. It may help where the GPU is the limit. If the game hangs or shows glitches with it on, turn it off.
- Measured on an RTX 5080 with a Ryzen 7 9800X3D, standing in the park in Seattle, in turn with the emulator at high priority, with 22-35% of the CPU taken by other programs.
